dietEvidence.body: The short snout, jaws and teeth indicate herbivory. No gut contents are known; the plants eaten and the feeding posture remain unknown.

sizeNote: Length and mass are estimates from incomplete material, not measurements of a whole animal.
tagline: An early stegosaur with small plates and a relatively short snout. It helps document the early evolution of the stegosaur body plan.
summary: An early stegosaur with small plates and a relatively short snout. It helps document the early evolution of the stegosaur body plan.

discovery.body: Named by Dong, Tang & Zhou, 1982. The record is known from Shaximiao Formation, Sichuan. Several partial skeletons, including a skull.

fossilEvidence.title: Preserved material
fossilEvidence.body: The species is known from skull and postcranial material from the Shaximiao Formation of Sichuan. The hypodigm includes multiple individuals but not a complete growth series.

fossilEvidence.title: Stratigraphic and geographic occurrence
fossilEvidence.body: Shaximiao Formation, Sichuan records the species in the Middle Jurassic. The numeric range used here is ≈168–161 Ma, an occurrence estimate rather than a direct date on every specimen.

anatomy.title: Preserved anatomy
anatomy.body: The skull is relatively short-snouted and less derived than those of later stegosaurs. The postcranium bears small dorsal plates and at least one pair of tail spines.

behaviour.body: No direct evidence of social or display behaviour. The small dorsal plates and tail spines are preserved; their function in display, thermoregulation or defence is not established.

reconstruction.body: A licensed life reconstruction is assigned to this record and credited in Sources and credits. The species is known from several partial skeletons, including a skull. The reconstruction is an artist's interpretation of appearance, not a direct observation from the fossil record; preserved integument, where present, is described in the anatomy section, and the soft-tissue outline is otherwise inferred.

confidenceNote: Huayangosaurus is known from skull and postcranial material from the Middle Jurassic Shaximiao Formation. It is usually placed outside Stegosauridae as a basal stegosaur, but the family label is navigational. No gut contents are known.

primer.lead: Huayangosaurus taibaii was an early stegosaur from the [Middle Jurassic](/deep-time?period=jurassic) of Sichuan, China. It is one of the oldest well-known stegosaurs and helps document how the group’s plates and spines evolved.
paragraphs: The skull is relatively short-snouted and less derived than those of later stegosaurs. The postcranium bears small dorsal plates and at least one pair of tail spines. Huayangosaurus is usually placed outside Stegosauridae, as a basal stegosaur.

Its plant diet is inferred from the jaws and teeth. The function of the plates and spines — display, thermoregulation or defence — is not established, and there is no direct evidence of its social behaviour.
primer.takeaway: A small-plated early stegosaur from the Middle Jurassic.
